Data used in this study is quite old (2006). Since then several social, economic and political changes have been occurred in Egypt. I suggest actualizing data to better reflect present social situation in Egypt I order to better understand situation of Egyptian adolescents. This opinion is supported by the fact that the authors used actualize references (i.e.: 2012, 2013), and therefore is quite difficult to accept present results obtained at so long time ago from the present time.

Dr.  Josep Tur
Academic Editor, PeerJ

Dear Dr. Tur,
Thank you for your favorable review of our manuscript. The reviewers' comments were much appreciated, and my co-authors and I have revised our manuscript based on the feedback that was provided by the reviewers at PeerJ. To help in your second review of the manuscript, I have inserted the original reviewer comments and provided an explanation (in red text) of what action was taken in response to the comment. We hope that you will agree that these revisions have resulted in a stronger version of our manuscript.
Thank you again for your consideration of our manuscript. We look forward to hearing from you and your team regarding the final decision on our manuscript for publication in PeerJ.

Sincerely,

Karen L. Celedonia
















Editor's comments
Major.Data used in this study is quite old (2006). Since then several social, economic and political changes have been occurred in Egypt. I suggest actualizing data to better reflect present social situation in Egypt I order to better understand situation of Egyptian adolescents. This opinion is supported by the fact that the authors used actualize references (i.e.: 2012, 2013), and therefore is quite difficult to accept present results obtained at so long time ago from the present time.
The authors very much agree with the fact that the data used in this study is dated and does not reflect recent social and political changes in Egypt. Upon careful review of the literature however, there were no peer-reviewed studies which treated the subject of interpersonal violence among Egyptian adolescents or related risk behaviors. This paucity in literature was a problem until relatively recently hence the use of recent citations.Minor.Introduction is too long. It must be shortened at least to 1 and half page.
We have shortened the Introduction.
Methods.Authors must state why the student response rate is 87%.
Language has been added in the second paragraph of the Methods section explaining why the response rate was so high.
Authors also stated that this is a self-reported study. Did the authors some validation to be sure that the self-reported method is yields appropriate results? If authors use a validated methods, please, give appropriate reference.
Language has been added in the second paragraph of the Methods section answering this question.DiscussionAuthors must declare in limitations of the study that this is a cross-sectional study, and then no relationships cause-effect can be done.
We have added language in the discussion that addresses this issue.
Reviewer Comments
Reviewer 1
Comments for the author
Introduction1. “40%” instead of “40 percent”; and “70%” instead of “70 percent”.
We have applied this modification.
2. The manuscript would benefit is the authors could include page 3 of the introduction section, lines 1-4 and lines 7-11 in a “limitations and strengths” section.
We have applied this modification.
Methods1. The manuscript would benefit if the authors include a table detailing the information on the data variables created.
This table was created, and is referred to as Table 1; it has also been uploaded.
2. The manuscript would benefit if the authors detail “anxiety and signs of depression” as individual-level variables separately.
We have applied this modification.
3. Please, remove “for Linux (www.linuxmint.com)”.
Removed per request. There may be subtle differences in the way Stata performs or interprets syntax on different platforms which was why we initially included it. Full reproducibility of results often requires having each stage of the process and tools used detailed.
Results1. Page 1 of the “Results” section: “The mean age of the sample was 13.2 years old” instead of “The mean age of the sample was 13.2 years”.
We have applied this modification.
2. Why the authors included “food insecurity” without discussing this variable?
 Food insecurity was included as a rough indicator of socioeconomic status to see if its inclusion in the regressions adjusted any of the regression coefficients/odds ratios. In most studies, as SES is known to influence behavioral outcomes, we included this in order to be in line with existing studies.
3. Please, change “Table 3” for “Table 2”.
We have applied this modification. But due to the addition of 2 new tables, these tables have different table numbers now. Old Table 3 is now Table 4, and old Table 2 is now Table 5.
4. The manuscript would benefit including a table assessing males and females separately since females were less likely than males to be involved in physical fights.
This table has been added, and is Labeled as "Table 3."

onally, the effects of urbanization have led to increased migration from urban areas
to surrounding rural areas, creating pockets of impoverished, suburban populations – situations
which have been shown to increase aggressive and violent behavior among adolescents
(Schnieders et al., 2003; Carlson, 2006)
However, even within these turbulent environments, not all adolescents exhibit violent behavior,
indicating that there may be other, micro-level factors that are exerting influence either as risk or
protective factors. A better understanding of individual and social correlates of violence among
adolescents in LMICs is important to violence prevention initiatives in these countries: this
knowledge can be used to guide the development of early interventions meant to attenuate risk
factors for participation in violent behavior. With rates of non-fatal injuries resulting from
violent behavior starting to increase during mid-adolescence (age 14 years) and violence peaking
during late adolescence (Odero & Kibosia, 1995; Butchart et al., 1997; DHHS, 2001), violence
prevention programs geared towards adolescents are critical to protecting the well-being of the
present generation as well as laying the foundation for a more peaceful future.
